newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish forestries fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Finnish forestries fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Finnish forestry groups UPM-Kymmene, Enso and Metsa-Serla fell sharply on Wednesday as investors took profits after recent gains, brokers said.
At 1605/1405 GMT, Finland's biggest forestry group UPM traded at 110.50 markka, down 4.50 markka or almost four percent. Trade was a moderate 37 million markka.
Enso's more liquid R share traded at 44.50 markka, down 1.40 markka or more than three percent. Trade was a modest 13 million markka.
Metsa-Serla's more liquid B share was at 40.00 markka, down 2.90 markka or more than six percent. Trade was a thin four million markka.
"There is nothing special in forestries ... players are just taking profits," a broker said.

By the market's closing on Tuesday, the Helsinki bourse's forest industry sub-index had risen 21 percent since the turn of the year. The HEX all-share index hit an all-time high 3,017.54 points -- up 21 percent on end-1996 -- on Thursday.
At 1605/1405 GMT, the forestry index was 3.7 percent lower and the HEX just under one percent down on Tuesday's close.
